definition: In this source, a dissociative pattern refers to a distinct, differentiated pattern of activity across ventral hippocampus subregions seen when a trauma reminder is recalled. This pattern was linked to basolateral amygdala activation, suggesting coordinated but non-uniform neural responses during intrusive emotional memory retrieval.

reasons: The phrase “intrusive emotional memory retrieval” is not stated in the packet; the source only describes recollection of a trauma reminder and notes that intrusive recollections are often triggered by trauma reminders.

“Coordinated but non-uniform neural responses” is an interpretive generalization beyond the packet’s wording, which only reports a positive correlation between VH sub-region activation and BLA activation.

The definition’s claim that the BLA link “suggest[es] coordinated but non-uniform neural responses” goes beyond the packet, which only states that the “dissociative pattern of activation of the VH sub-regions positively correlated with the activation of the BLA,” without explicitly characterizing coordination or non-uniformity.

The definition frames the neural activity as occurring “during intrusive emotional memory retrieval.” While the packet discusses intrusive recollections generally and describes the experimental “re-exposed to the context of the trauma” paradigm, it does not explicitly label the task/activation as “intrusive emotional memory retrieval.”
